info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package billing is your org's balance, what it has spent, and the cards it pays with.

get.summary: Answers the caller's billing accounts: the org itself, its currency, when it was opened, and the caller's own standing in it.
get.description:
Answers the caller's billing accounts: the org itself, its currency, when it
was opened, and the caller's own standing in it.

The standing is the caller's, resolved from the validated principal here and
sent to the store rather than looked up there — the membership roster is IAM's
and commerce keeps none, so a callee that answered "what role is this" would
be inventing it. An anonymous read gets the account with no role rather than
an implied membership.

Scoped to the caller's own org, which is the whole tenancy story: there is no
org field on the wire and none on the input.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers one billing account's roster.
get.description:
Answers one billing account's roster.

commerce stores no roster — that is IAM's — so the only member it can name is
the caller, and that is what comes back. What it does enforce is that the
account named in the path is the caller's own: a foreign id is 403, not an
empty list, because "no members" and "not your account" are different answers.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the billing account id, which for this store is the org's own id.

get.summary: Lists this org's spend caps: the ceiling, its scope, whether it enforces, and how much of it has been spent this period.
get.description:
Lists this org's spend caps: the ceiling, its scope, whether it enforces, and
how much of it has been spent this period.

`periodSpentCents`, `over` and `warn` are ABSENT rather than zero when the
spend could not be read, because "nothing spent" and "spend unknown" are
different answers and a customer acting on the first when the second is true
would be reading a ceiling that is not there. The policy row is reported
either way.

The period is the UTC calendar month and `resetsAt` is when the count starts
again, so a surface can say "resets on" without a second call.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

post.summary: Opens a spend cap on the caller's own org.
post.description:
Opens a spend cap on the caller's own org.

At least one limit must mean something: a threshold above zero (a spend cap)
or a requests-per-minute above zero (a rate limit). A row that bounds neither
is refused rather than stored, because a ceiling nothing measures against is a
ceiling a customer believes in and does not have.

The cap is keyed on the caller's own billing subject, resolved server-side —
the SAME key the verdict looks it up under, which is what makes enforcement
bind rather than merely record.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers whether one proposed spend fits inside this org's caps.
get.description:
Answers whether one proposed spend fits inside this org's caps.

It is the per-request verdict the metering edge consumes before every priced
call, and its caller is a SERVICE rather than a person: the platform, stating
the org over the plane, with no user behind it. So this admits that principal
where the CRUD beside it does not.

Every covering row is evaluated, most-restrictive-wins, and the tightest one
is what `capCents`, `spentCents` and `reason` describe. Soft rows never deny;
nor does a project-scoped enforcing row whose project axis the caller could
not establish — `pv=1` is how a caller states that it did, and an unproven
claim must not be able to refuse traffic.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows the verdict to one project's caps. Empty is the org-wide row.

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: Service narrows it to one service's caps. Empty is every service.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount is the proposed spend in cents.

parameters.name: pv
parameters.description:
PV is "1" when the caller ESTABLISHED the project rather than merely
carrying a claim of one. An unproven project may not deny traffic.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller's spend caps and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller's spend caps and answers 204.

Removing a cap RAISES what the org may spend, so it takes the same authority
setting one does. The caps that remain still bind: this drops one, never the
whole policy.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the cap to remove, from the path.

patch.summary: Changes one spend cap: raise or lower the ceiling, flip enforcement, retune the rate limit.
patch.description:
Changes one spend cap: raise or lower the ceiling, flip enforcement, retune
the rate limit.

Only the fields the body carries move. Every mutable field is optional, and an
absent one is PRESERVED rather than reset — so a change that flips enforcement
cannot silently wipe the threshold it enforces.

A cap belonging to another org is a 404, not a 403: a guessed id must not
become an oracle for what anyone else holds.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers the spendable prepaid balance of the wallet this caller bills from — the same wallet the AI prepaid gate reads before admitting a paid request, the edge meter debits, and a top-up or admin grant credits.
get.description:
Answers the spendable prepaid balance of the wallet this caller bills from — the same
wallet the AI prepaid gate reads before admitting a paid request, the edge meter
debits, and a top-up or admin grant credits.

The wallet is an ADDRESS, not an org: `account` echoes the key resolved within the
ledger — the org's shared pool for a tenant org, a personal account for a member of
the shared signup org.

`balance`, `holds` and `available` are whole USD cents, floored from the ledger's
exact 18-decimal value. `cash`, `line` and `credit` say where `available` came from,
and add up to it; `prepaid` is `cash` plus `line`.

Scoped to the caller's own org from the validated IAM principal (401 without one).
A balance that cannot be read is 502, never 0: unknown is not broke.

get.summary: What is for sale in dollars and how it is paid for
get.description:
Answers the plans on sale on the host's brand, the credit packs, and the payment types the org's processors take now (`shared_payment_token`, and `stablecoin` with the networks a deposit may use), as `{version, currency, plans, creditPacks, payment, links}`.

PUBLIC. A caller with no credential is served, and the catalog is the brand the request host names; one shared copy serves every anonymous reader. A caller with a credential is answered for its own org's processors and is never served the shared copy.

post.summary: Opens a checkout for exactly one item, USD credit (`kind: "credit"`, `usdCents`) or a plan's first period (`kind: "plan"`, `plan`, `interval`), and answers it priced as the sale prices it.
post.description:
Opens a checkout for exactly one item, USD credit (`kind: "credit"`, `usdCents`) or a
plan's first period (`kind: "plan"`, `plan`, `interval`), and answers it priced as the
sale prices it. Nothing is charged: a checkout is paid by completing it.

The checkout is the caller's own, and only the caller reads, changes or pays it.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers where one of the caller's own checkouts stands: open, pending, complete or failed, with the next step while it waits on the buyer and the order once it is complete.
get.description:
Answers where one of the caller's own checkouts stands: open, pending, complete or
failed, with the next step while it waits on the buyer and the order once it is
complete. A checkout waiting on a stablecoin deposit is completed here once the deposit
has been credited. A checkout that is not the caller's is 404.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the checkout, as the open call answered it.

patch.summary: Replaces the item of one of the caller's checkouts that is still open, or failed, and prices it again.
patch.description:
Replaces the item of one of the caller's checkouts that is still open, or failed, and
prices it again. A checkout that is pending or complete can no longer be changed (409).

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the checkout, from the path.

post.summary: Pays one of the caller's checkouts with a shared payment token the buyer granted the agent (`{"payment":{"type":"shared_payment_token","token":"spt_..."}}`) or with a stablecoin deposit (`{"payment":{"type":"stablecoin","network":"base"}}`), and answers the checkout under the status the attempt earned.
post.description:
Pays one of the caller's checkouts with a shared payment token the buyer granted the
agent (`{"payment":{"type":"shared_payment_token","token":"spt_..."}}`) or with a
stablecoin deposit (`{"payment":{"type":"stablecoin","network":"base"}}`), and answers
the checkout under the status the attempt earned.

200 is complete, with the order. 202 waits on the buyer, and `next` says what to do: send
the deposit, or take the bank's step. A refusal is 402 for a payment that was declined and
400, 404, 409, 422 or 429 for the rest, always with `error.code` to branch on.

The `Idempotency-Key` header is required. It binds the charge to this checkout, the buyer
and the key, so completing twice is one purchase; the same key answers the same order, and
another key on a checkout already paid is 409.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the checkout, from the path.

get.summary: Answers what the caller can spend right now, one entry per currency.
get.description:
Answers what the caller can spend right now, one entry per currency.

Only ACTIVE grants count: a voided, exhausted or lapsed grant contributes
nothing, which is why this number can be smaller than the grant list suggests
and why the two reads exist separately. It is credit, not prepaid balance —
/v1/billing/balance is the wallet, and the two are added by the gate, never by
a reader.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers that same spendable credit split by grant tag, with the earliest expiry under each and the total across all of them.
get.description:
Answers that same spendable credit split by grant tag, with the earliest
expiry under each and the total across all of them.

The split is the point: it is how trial credit is told apart from bought
credit, which is what a surface asks before it decides whether to spend any.
An unregistered address answers 404 and a caller reads that as "no credit", so
this being served is the difference between a customer with a trial grant
being offered their trial and being told they have none.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Lists the caller's credit grants — every one of them, spent and lapsed and voided included.
get.description:
Lists the caller's credit grants — every one of them, spent and lapsed and
voided included.

That is deliberate and it is what makes the list useful: a grant list is a
LEDGER, and one that hid its spent rows could not be reconciled against a
burn-down. What is spendable right now is the sibling read, /v1/billing/
credit-balance, and the two are different questions.

Scoped to the caller's own wallet, resolved server-side.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

post.summary: Issues a deposit address the caller can send crypto to, on the asset they ask for.
post.description:
Issues a deposit address the caller can send crypto to, on the asset they ask
for.

The address credits the CALLER'S own wallet and nobody else's: the payer is
the validated principal, never a body value. Asking again reuses the caller's
open intent rather than minting a second address, so a refresh cannot spray
key generations — and a payer who sent to the address they saw earlier is
still credited.

No balance moves here. The chain watcher credits on real confirmations, so
what comes back is an address, a status and the terms: the minimum that
credits, any fee, the confirmations required, and one line of instructions.
Once the transfer is that deep the deposit is credited as cash to the caller's
balance (GET /v1/billing/balance, cash) and its status is succeeded.

The asset is checked against GET /v1/billing/crypto/options before anything is
minted. A chain, a token or a pair the rail does not accept is 400, and the
answer lists the accepted chains, tokens and assets. A deposit rail with
nothing watched is 503 — nothing sent now can be credited, and the Gateway
rail or a card is the way to pay until it reopens.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Reads one of the caller's own deposit intents back — pending, confirming, or succeeded.
get.description:
Reads one of the caller's own deposit intents back — pending, confirming, or
succeeded.

status is pending until a transfer to the address is seen, confirming while
the chain buries it (confirmations counts up to requiredConfirmations), and
succeeded once it is credited: creditedCents is then in the caller's balance
as cash (GET /v1/billing/balance, cash). The answer is the same shape the mint
returned, terms and instructions included, so polling it is all an agent needs.

An intent belonging to another payer answers 404, exactly as an id that names
nothing, so a guessed id cannot confirm that somebody else's deposit exists.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the deposit intent id.

get.summary: Answers the terms to sign a USDC top-up against, for an agent or a person paying from a wallet: the treasury to pay, the networks and USDC contracts, the EIP-712 domain and types, the limits, and a nonce issued to the caller.
get.description:
Answers the terms to sign a USDC top-up against, for an agent or a person
paying from a wallet: the treasury to pay, the networks and USDC contracts,
the EIP-712 domain and types, the limits, and a nonce issued to the caller.

Sign TransferWithAuthorization {from, to: payTo, value, validAfter,
validBefore, nonce} under one network's domain, then POST it here with the
salt. The nonce is the caller's own: a payment signed against it credits the
caller and cannot be presented by anyone else.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

post.summary: Takes a signed USDC payment from the caller's Circle Gateway balance to the treasury, and answers what became of it.
post.description:
Takes a signed USDC payment from the caller's Circle Gateway balance to the
treasury, and answers what became of it.

accepted: Circle Gateway LOCKED the USDC and the caller is credited — or,
once the caller holds $1,000 of credit Gateway has not confirmed, credited
when Gateway confirms this payment (deferred). pending: the outcome is not
known yet; read it back or present the same payment again — it resolves to
one credit either way. A refusal is 4xx with Gateway's reason
(insufficient_balance, invalid_signature, …) or ours (nonce_not_issued,
recipient_mismatch, amount_below_minimum, …); 503 means the rail is shut.

Who is credited is the caller, never a body value: the payer is resolved
server-side, and the payment's own nonce must be the one issued to it.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Reads one of the caller's own USDC top-ups back: pending, accepted (credited or deferred), settled, failed or refused.
get.description:
Reads one of the caller's own USDC top-ups back: pending, accepted (credited
or deferred), settled, failed or refused.

A payment belonging to another payer answers 404, exactly as an id that names
nothing, so a guessed id cannot confirm somebody else's payment exists.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the top-up's id, from the path.

get.summary: Answers which chains and tokens the crypto rail accepts — what an asset picker renders — and the pairs themselves in assets: a chain and a token each on offer are not a pair on offer.
get.description:
Answers which chains and tokens the crypto rail accepts — what an asset picker
renders — and the pairs themselves in assets: a chain and a token each on offer
are not a pair on offer.

It is the intersection of two live facts rather than a configured list: an
asset appears only if something is WATCHING it and the custody processor
supports it. An address nobody watches credits nobody, so offering one would
take a customer's money and lose it. A rail with nothing armed answers 503,
not an empty menu — "no rail" and "no assets" are different, and only one of
them means try again later.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers where the purchase surface is and what it speaks: its version, the paths of its parts, the checkout's verbs in order, the payment types a checkout completes with, and how a subscription is renewed by an agent.
get.description:
Answers where the purchase surface is and what it speaks: its version, the paths of its
parts, the checkout's verbs in order, the payment types a checkout completes with, and
how a subscription is renewed by an agent.

PUBLIC. A caller with no credential is served, and one shared copy serves every
anonymous reader.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Lists the caller's invoices, newest first, with the count beside them.
get.description:
Lists the caller's invoices, newest first, with the count beside them.

It is scoped to the caller's own billing subject — the wallet this request
bills from, resolved server-side — so a query cannot widen it to another
customer of the same org. An org with no invoices is an empty list, not a
refusal.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

post.summary: Raise a draft invoice against a customer
post.description:
Raises a DRAFT invoice against a customer in the caller's own org. It is the
org admin's act; a member is refused 403.

The invoice is not collectible yet: a draft exists so it can be read and
corrected, and issueInvoice is the separate act that turns it into a demand for
payment. The subtotal and amount due are computed from the lines, so there is
no total to send and none to get wrong.

The billing org is the caller's, taken from the validated principal, so an
invoice can only ever be raised on the caller's own books.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Is the order invoice a link shows, read on the brand of the host it is asked on: a link read on another brand's host is a miss.
get.description:
Is the order invoice a link shows, read on the brand of the host
it is asked on: a link read on another brand's host is a miss.

get.summary: Is the order invoice a link shows, as a PDF to print or save.
get.description: Is the order invoice a link shows, as a PDF to print or save.

get.summary: Read one invoice
get.description:
Reads one invoice out of the caller's org.

The org scopes the read by construction — the store is namespaced to it — so an
id belonging to another tenant is not found rather than found and then filtered.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice id.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description:
Brand is the brand that bills (hanzo, lux, zoo, pars), whose mark and
address a rendered invoice carries. The edge sets it from the caller's
issuer; empty is Hanzo.

post.summary: Pays one of the caller's past-due renewals with a fresh shared payment token.
post.description:
Pays one of the caller's past-due renewals with a fresh shared payment token. The token
becomes the subscription's payment method when it carries a recurring interval that
covers the renewal, and the invoice is charged on it now.

200 is paid. 402 is declined, with `error.code` to branch on, and the subscription keeps
the method it had. An invoice that is not the caller's is 404.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice or the subscription, from the path.

post.summary: Collect an issued invoice from credits, balance, then card
post.description:
Collects an issued invoice: credit grants first, then prepaid balance, then the
card on file — the same waterfall the dunning workflow runs. It spends the
named customer's money, so it is the org admin's act; a member is refused 403.

A DECLINE IS NOT AN ERROR. It answers with paid=false, a reason, and the
invoice still open, because a declined collection is a normal business outcome
that must remain retryable — and because sealing it as a failure would wedge
dunning behind a replayed decline. Only a successful collection is sealed, so a
retry of a paid invoice replays the receipt instead of charging again.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice id.

post.summary: Issue a draft invoice, making it collectible
post.description:
Issues a draft invoice: moves it to OPEN, assigns its number, and makes it
collectible. It is the org admin's act; a member is refused 403.

Only a draft can be issued. An invoice already open, paid or void is refused
with the state machine's own reason rather than being silently re-issued, which
would mint a second number for one debt.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice id.

post.summary: Pay an invoice with the buyer present
post.description:
Pays an open invoice with the buyer present. A paid or declined payment answers 200
with the invoice and, for a decline, the reason. A card the bank asks to
authenticate answers 402 with what the buyer finishes (code, id, clientSecret,
publishableKey, quote, message). Paying twice is one payment.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice id.

get.summary: Download one invoice as a PDF
get.description:
Answers the invoice as an attachment — `application/pdf` under a Content-Disposition naming the invoice number — rather than as a JSON value, which is why this one route is untyped where its five siblings are typed: a PDF is bytes with a filename, and the two headers are the whole contract.

The render is a PURE function of the invoice: one page, no timestamps and no random ids, so the same invoice renders the same bytes however often it is asked for and a retry after a dropped connection costs a re-render and nothing else.

The invoice is read from the caller's own org, taken from the VALIDATED IAM owner claim and never from a client header, and the lookup is scoped at the storage layer — so an id belonging to another customer resolves to nothing and answers 404 rather than being found and then refused.

post.summary: Void a draft or issued invoice
post.description:
Voids a draft or issued invoice — the cancel. It is the org admin's act; a
member is refused 403.

A paid invoice cannot be voided: money has moved, and the correction for that
is a refund, not an erasure. The state machine refuses it and that refusal is
the answer.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the invoice id.

get.summary: Answers the org's own postings inside `range=`, each as a signed entry: a DEPOSIT CREDITS the wallet (positive, account `credits:<org>`), a HOLD sets money aside for a payment agreed and not yet made (negative, account `held:<org>`) and its return gives it back (positive), and every other posting DEBITS it (negative, account `usage:<org>`), described by its notes or its tags.
get.description:
Answers the org's own postings inside `range=`, each as a signed
entry: a DEPOSIT CREDITS the wallet (positive, account `credits:<org>`), a
HOLD sets money aside for a payment agreed and not yet made (negative, account
`held:<org>`) and its return gives it back (positive), and every other posting
DEBITS it (negative, account `usage:<org>`), described by its notes or its
tags. The sign is the posting's own meaning, read through ONE
vocabulary shared with the ledger that wrote it — a reader with its own
spelling for `deposit` rendered a customer's grant as a charge.

This is the closest projection of the truth. The org's double-entry postings
are the source of record — balanced, only ever appended, one file per org —
and this lane is that list, wider than either half of it: the deposits are the
grants /v1/billing/credits lists and the debits are the spend /v1/billing/usage
rolls up. It answers 503 where this deployment runs no ledger, rather than
reporting an empty wallet.

A row whose timestamp will not parse is KEPT rather than dropped — a malformed
date must show up in a money list, not vanish from it. `balanceCents` is
omitted: these are MOVEMENTS, and the standing balance is /v1/billing/balance.

Cents are ROUNDED from the ledger's exact 18-decimal USD. Scoped to the
caller's own org, where the org's ledger file is the tenant boundary; 401
without a validated principal.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description:
Range is the window: 24h, 7d, 30d or 90d. Anything else — including
absent — is 30d, so a typo silently widens the window to a month rather
than failing.

delete.description:
Stops using a linked plan.

Without a query it ends the link of the org you act in: an owner or admin of the org
may, and so may the person who holds the account the plan is lent from. With
`from=<account>` it ends the link that account's plan is lent through, from whatever
org you act in — so someone removed from the borrowing org can still take their plan
back — and `from` must be one of your own `plans`. Ending a link frees the plan to be
lent again. Answers 404 when nothing is linked and 403 when it is not yours to end. It
is on the audit trail.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: The plan this org borrows, and the plans you could lend it
get.description:
Answers the plan the org you act in borrows, and the plans you could lend it.

`link` is the plan this org uses, omitted when it uses none; `live` is false once the
plan it was lent from has lapsed, and the link then confers nothing. Any member of the
org may read it. `plans` is every live paid plan YOU hold — your own wallet in the
shared signup org and each org you own — whoever else is in the org, with `org` naming
the org one is already lent to. `canLink` and `canUnlink` say what you may do from
here, by the rules the writes enforce: link a plan if you are an owner or admin of an
org that may borrow, holds no live paid plan of its own and borrows none; end the link
if you are an owner or admin of the org or hold the plan it is lent from.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

put.summary: Use a plan you hold on this org
put.description:
Uses a plan you hold on the org you act in.

The whole org is covered by it, and one plan is lent to at most one org. You must be
an owner or admin of the org, and `from` must be one of your own `plans`: your own
wallet in the shared signup org, or an org you own. The org keeps its own wallet and
its own included allowance; a plan lent to it is never its to cancel. Refusals: 403
when you are not an owner or admin; 400 `no_plan_to_link` when `from` is not a live
paid plan you hold; 400 `org_cannot_link` for the shared signup org, a held or reserved
org, or the plan's own org; 409 `org_has_plan` when the org already holds a live paid
plan of its own; 409 `plan_already_linked` when the plan is lent to another org; 409
`org_already_linked` when the org already uses one. It is on the audit trail.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Cards and accounts on file for the caller
get.description:
Answers every payment method the caller has saved, newest first.

A saved method is a card or account VAULTED at the processor: what is stored here is the processor's token for it plus the last four digits and the expiry a customer recognises it by, never a card number.

The list is the caller's OWN — the wallet this request bills from, resolved server-side — so a query cannot widen it to another customer of the same org.

`/v1/billing/portal/methods` answers the same list under the name a hosted checkout addresses it by. One set of rows, two spellings; a card added at either is present at both.

A store that cannot be read answers an EMPTY LIST rather than a failure: the saved-cards panel renders empty instead of breaking the page around it.

post.summary: Save a card or account for the caller
post.description:
Vaults the instrument at the processor and stores the row.

A saved method is a card or account VAULTED at the processor: what is stored here is the processor's token for it plus the last four digits and the expiry a customer recognises it by, never a card number.

The list is the caller's OWN — the wallet this request bills from, resolved server-side — so a query cannot widen it to another customer of the same org.

`/v1/billing/portal/methods` answers the same list under the name a hosted checkout addresses it by. One set of rows, two spellings; a card added at either is present at both.

Saving a card ALREADY on file answers with the row that already holds it rather than stacking a duplicate — 200 for that, 201 for a genuinely new row, so a client can tell which happened. A card the processor declines is 402 and nothing is stored.

The org's cards are an admin's to add: a member billed from the org's account is refused 403 with a sentence naming who to ask. A member billed from a wallet of their own saves cards to that wallet.

delete.summary: Removes one card or account the caller has saved.
delete.description:
Removes one card or account the caller has saved.

Nothing is reserved by a quote. Without the parameter the catalog is unchanged.

It is public and needs no tenant, and it is the catalog of the brand the request's host resolves to — the same brand `/v1/commerce/org` answers there. A brand that publishes no plans answers an empty list.

put.description:
Sets the auto-reload rule of the wallet the caller pays from, and answers with the
rule as stored.

The org's own account's rule is its admins' to change, and the platform's; a
member billed from a wallet of their own (a person in the signup org) changes that
wallet's rule and no other (403 otherwise, with the plain sentence "Only an admin
of <org> can change its auto-reload. Ask an admin to do it."): the sweep charges
the payer's default card with nobody there.

ENABLING REQUIRES A CARD ON FILE (400), because the sweep charges off-session:
a rule naming no chargeable method is a promise the schedule cannot keep. The
amount is a top-up's own range, $5 to $5,000, and the balance it reloads below
is $0 to $5,000; a value outside either is refused the same way, the range in
the sentence. The sweep reloads at most `perDay` times in a UTC day.

The rule is the payer's OWN. The org and the wallet come from the validated
principal and the body names neither, so there is no field a write could be
steered through onto another payer's schedule.

The answer explains a sweep that charged nobody as readily as one that

post.summary: Buy a plan with a card
post.description:
Vaults the card (or reuses one already on file), charges the plan's FIRST period at the catalog price, and opens the subscription — one act, all of it server-side.

There is NO AMOUNT in the request. `level` picks which of the plan's published prices to buy at — an index, never a number — so what the card is charged is decided by the catalog and underpaying cannot be expressed.

`interval` picks the term: "month" (the default) or "year", which charges the plan's annual total now and renews yearly. A plan with no annual price refuses "year".

`lines` are a team's other seat types, bought on the same subscription: `[{"planId":"team-premium","quantity":1}]` beside `planId` "team" and `quantity` 1 is a team of one standard and one premium seat, charged both seats' prices. A team is at least two members across every seat type and at most 100; a line of a plan that is not a seat type of the team is 400 before any card is charged.

`coupon` is a plan coupon code (case-insensitive) for a percent off the FIRST month only; renewals bill the catalog price. It is a code, never an amount. A code that is unknown, expired, used up, not for this plan, or sent with annual billing or prepaid credit is 400, and one this org or this card has already redeemed is 409 — before any card is charged, never a silent full-price sale. The receipt names the coupon and its percent.

`wallet: true` says `sourceId` is a wallet's single-use token (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App Pay). The first period is authorized on the wallet, any coupon is held against the org and the card behind it, and only then is the payment captured; a coupon already used by either voids the hold and is 409. Cash App Pay names no card, so a coupon with it is 400. The token is kept nowhere, so the plan renews only once a card plan follows it: a plan's period is charged to a card on file, never to the prepaid balance, which pays for usage. A `sourceId` of "balance" or "credits" is 400 `plan_needs_card`.

Bought while the account holds a plan paid outside checkout (a wire, a comp) or one the balance used to renew, the card plan starts when that plan ends: the card is kept now and charged then, nothing is charged today, and the receipt states `startsAt`, `startsCents` and `follows`.

`balanceCents` is an organization's starting usage balance, bought in the same payment as the seats: `amountCents` is seats x price plus it, the invoice holds the seats and the balance is credited to the organization's prepaid balance (`balanceCents`, `balanceId` on the receipt). It is whole dollars and at most the plan's `limits.balanceCeiling`; one that is not, a plan that states no ceiling, or a balance sent with a wallet token or on a plan that starts later is 400 before any card is charged. A plan whose limits state how an organization orders it (spend limits, balance months, a ceiling) is bought only for the organization, by its admin, on a request that selects it with X-Org-Id; one that selects none is 400 ("choose the organization to buy for") before any card is charged. Whether the buyer administers it is asked of IAM at the sale, not read off the token: 403 when IAM no longer names them an admin, 503 when it cannot answer.

`consent` is the choice the checkout page holds, as @hanzo/event spells it ("analytics,marketing,ads"). The sale reaches an ad platform only under it. It counts only from a browser (a request with Sec-Fetch-Site), and a browser that sends GPC or DNT has allowed nothing, whatever the page says.

A fresh sale answers 201 with the receipt. An identical retry answers 200 with the FIRST sale's body, byte for byte, so a client cannot read a replay as a second subscription having been opened. A caller already on a paid plan is 409 rather than charged again.

The org's plan is bought only by an admin of the org or the platform: a member billed from the org's account is refused 403, before any card is charged, with a sentence naming who to ask. A member billed from a wallet of their own buys a plan for that wallet.

post.summary: Order a plan by invoice, paid by wire
post.description:
Raises an OPEN invoice for an organization's order — the seats at the plan's price and the starting balance — and sends it to the buyer. NOTHING STARTS until it is paid: "Your plan starts when we confirm your payment."

The body is a card sale's less the card and the coupon: `planId`, `quantity`, `lines`, `interval`, `balanceCents`. The organization is the one chosen with X-Org-Id (none chosen is 400), and only its admin, as IAM says now, orders (403). The answer carries the invoice, the amount due, the due date (the plan's `limits.invoiceDays`), when it is voided if unpaid (`limits.graceDays` later), the receiving bank with the reference to send exactly, the same as `howToPay` steps one field to a line, and `hostedUrl` and `pdfUrl`. A plan already paid for, or one with an invoice still open, is 409; a site that takes no order by invoice is 503. A retry under the same X-Idempotency-Key answers the same order as it stands at 200, with a new link and the bank read again; nothing is mailed again.

post.description:
Ends a subscription.

It cancels at the END OF THE PAID PERIOD by default, because a customer who
cancels has already paid for the period they are in and taking it away is
taking money for nothing. `atPeriodEnd: false` ends it at once, which is the
caller asking for that.

The org's plan is its admins' to end, and the platform's in support mode. A
member is refused with 403 and told to ask an admin; a member billed from a
wallet of their own may end that wallet's plan. Every one is on the audit
trail, the operator named when it is the platform acting inside the org.

A subscription from another org, or held by a wallet the caller may not
change, is not found rather than refused, so an id cannot be probed for
existence.

Resuming the org's plan commits its card to the next renewal, so it takes the

a reader knows there is more to ask for, and `user` echoes the wallet the page

get.summary: Reads one ledger entry by its id.
get.description:
Reads one ledger entry by its id.

It is the MEMBER of the collection beside it rather than a second way to ask —
the same rows GET /v1/billing/transactions lists, addressed one at a time. A
top-up receipt is read here, because a receipt IS a ledger entry: the id this
takes is the `transactionId` a top-up hands back.

The read is narrower than the list: commerce's core loads the row and refuses
anything that is not a deposit, so a row that exists but is not a top-up
answers 404. That asymmetry is stated rather than closed, because widening a
money read to make two shapes match is not a change worth making for symmetry.

The books are the caller's own and cannot be named, so a guessed id misses
rather than reaching another tenant's ledger.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Every billed call the caller's org made, attributed to a product
get.description:
Answers one row per BILLED call against the caller's org — transaction id, amount, timestamp and the metered unit. This is the raw charged ledger, not a rollup.

Each row is stamped with a canonical `metadata.product` derived from what the meter persisted: `agent` becomes agents, `provisioning` becomes the provisioned kind, a token-metered row becomes inference, anything else keeps its metering surface. The ledger has no product field of its own, so this read is where that dimension is made real — from the SAME charged rows, never a second meter. A row that already carries its own product WINS, so the derivation stops the day the meter records one.

Each row carries `name`: what its metered unit (`metadata.model`) reads as on a bill — `Desktop sandbox` for `desktop/visor`, `Agent sessions` for `session`. An AI model is its own name. Show `name`; `metadata.model` stays the unit the ledger keys on.

`product=<id>` filters to one product server-side. `groupBy=product` reduces to `{product,requests,amountCents}` rollups instead of rows.

`amount` is whole USD cents, ROUNDED; `decimal` beside it is the SAME debit exact, as an 18-decimal USD string. Sum `decimal`. A page of sub-cent token calls totals correctly there and totals ZERO in `amount` — that difference is real money.

Scoped to the caller's own org's books, where the org's ledger file IS the tenant boundary; no client-supplied subject is ever forwarded. 401 without a validated principal. The co-resident read returns the 2000 most recent debits, newest first; `start` and `end` narrow the window only on the split-deploy upstream.

post.summary: Debits one act an application metered to the org it acts for, and answers the receipt.
post.description:
Debits one act an application metered to the org it acts for, and
answers the receipt.

The caller is an application acting as itself — an IAM client_credentials
token — and the org is the one that token acts in: the application's own, or
one that granted it membership, selected with X-Org-Id and named again in
`org`. A person, an API key, an unauthenticated caller, and a body naming an
org the token does not act in are all refused before anything is debited.

The debit lands in the same ledger every other meter writes, in the wallet GET
/v1/billing/balance reports for the same caller. It is exactly-once on `id`: a
retry answers the same receipt, and the same id for a different amount is 409.
Recording does not gate — the work already happened — so a caller that must
refuse unfunded work asks GET /v1/billing/balance and GET
/v1/billing/alerts/authorize first.

get.summary: Answers per-account totals for the linked provider accounts the gateway ROUTED this caller's traffic through — requests, prompt and completion tokens, recorded cost — plus their honest sum.
get.description:
Answers per-account totals for the linked provider accounts the
gateway ROUTED this caller's traffic through — requests, prompt and completion
tokens, recorded cost — plus their honest sum.

This is the one read in the billing namespace scoped to the PERSON, not the
org. Rows are keyed on (validated org, validated user), so a caller sees the
accounts THEY linked and never a colleague's, even inside one org — everything
else under /v1/billing is org-wide. Neither key is ever read from the request
body or the query.

It is a ROUTING counter, not the money ledger. `costCents` is 0 for an account
billed by its own subscription, where the plan pays the provider directly, so
these totals do not reconcile against what the org was charged.
/v1/billing/usage is the charged ledger.

401 without a validated principal. Where the linked-account plane is not
resident the answer is an honest 501 — never an empty breakdown, which would
read as no usage.

get.summary: Answers the caller's month: what their plan includes, what has been consumed against it, and the wallet beside it.
get.description:
Answers the caller's month: what their plan includes, what has been consumed
against it, and the wallet beside it.

The two blocks are SEPARATE monies and are never added. One is usage a plan
granted; the other is prepaid credit bought with a card. Their sum is not a
number anyone holds, and a reader that formed it would be inventing a balance.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

get.summary: Answers where to send a wire top-up: the receiving bank details, with the caller's own payment reference.
get.description:
Answers where to send a wire top-up: the receiving bank details, with the
caller's own payment reference.

The account is the SERVING BRAND'S — resolved from the host the customer is
paying on, so paying on one brand never shows another's bank — and the
reference carries the caller's billing key, which is how an arriving wire
names who it credits. Nothing mints here; a receipt is settled by an operator
once the bank confirms it.

It is all-or-nothing: no configured account is 503 rather than a partial form,
because nobody can wire to three fields out of five.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

post.summary: Credits the wallet that holds a wire's reference with the cents the bank received, once.
post.description:
Credits the wallet that holds a wire's reference with the cents the bank received, once.
A reference nobody was given credits nothing (404), a repeat posts nothing and answers
`credited: false`, and a repeat for another amount is 409.

SuperAdmin only. Every reconcile is on the audit trail as wire.reconciled, naming who
attested the receipt, and recorded by commerce as a billing event.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

a promo, a coupon's month). Last, for the ZAP wire.

LineItems carries no omitempty and is never allocated empty, because the
wire it reproduces sends `null` for an invoice with no lines. An empty
array there would be a different answer to "were there lines".

BalanceCents is the subject's balance AFTER the charge settled, in cents, read
from the ledger GET /v1/billing/balance reads, so a caller does not have to

ProcessorRef is the payment processor's own reference. It is the only field
that proves money moved at the GATEWAY rather than merely in our ledger,
which is why it is answered and not only logged. Absent where the processor
returned none.

the HTTP status: the call succeeded whenever this field is present, and what
the PROCESSOR did is what this says.

Test states which bucket was credited — sandbox money or real money — so no
reader has to guess whether a receipt is real. Sandbox and live funds are
physically separate ledgers, and a reader that conflates them restates the
company's revenue.

transactionId.description:
TransactionID is the ledger entry this charge created. It is the handle a
later read or a refund names, and it is minted by the ledger rather than by
the caller.

Invoice is the invoice AFTER the attempt — its status is the authority on

no error is a DECLINE: the invoice stays open and may be collected again.

that proves money moved at the gateway rather than only in our ledger.

address is shared. Absent where the address alone names the payer.

address was asked for: a record of intent, not a quote. What is credited is
what arrives. Absent when nothing was named.

is seen.

cents, once it succeeded. A later transfer to the same address is credited
too, and shows in the balance rather than here.

depositAddress.description: DepositAddress is where to send it.

ExpiresAt is when this address stops being handed out again (RFC3339). A
transfer that arrives after it is still credited.

feeCents.description:
FeeCents is deducted from every deposit before it is credited: the cost of
sweeping it out of the custody address. Absent deducts nothing.

is credited.

Status is pending until a transfer to the address is seen, confirming while
the chain buries it, and succeeded once it is credited as cash in the
payer's balance (GET /v1/billing/balance, cash).

Assets is every (chain, token) pair the deposit-address rail accepts.

not a pair on offer, so a picker that crosses them can name an asset the
rail will refuse.

From is the account to lend, as `plans` lists it: "<org>/<name>" for your own
wallet, "<org>" for an org you own.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is the top-up amount in whole cents when PlanID is empty.

balanceCents.description: BalanceCents is an organization's optional starting usage balance.

coupon.description: Coupon is an optional plan coupon code for a monthly subscription.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO-4217 code (default usd).

interval.description: Interval selects the billing term ("month" or "year").

level.description: Level selects which published price level of the plan to buy.

lines.description: Lines are a team's additional seat types bought on the same subscription.

planId.description: PlanID is the plan slug when buying a plan's first period; empty for a top-up.

quantity.description: Quantity is the seat count for a per-seat plan.

storeId.description: StoreID scopes the plan catalog when set.

lines.description:
Lines are the team's other seat types and the seats of each:
[{"planId":"team-premium","quantity":2}]. A seat type of the team the
subscription does not hold yet is added.

quantity.description: Quantity is the seats of the subscription's own seat type; 0 keeps them.

amountCents.description: AmountCents, when given, asks for the quote of that many dollars of credit.

country.description: Country is the buyer's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country; the edge's geo country when absent.

currency.description: Currency is what the checkout is paid in; usd when absent.

method.description: Method is how the buyer chose to pay, when they have (card, cash_app, pix, ...).

authorization.description:
Authorization is the EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization as signed: every
field a string, addresses and nonce 0x hex, value in USDC base units.

network.description:
Network is the CAIP-2 network the payment was signed for, one of the
terms' accepts, e.g. "eip155:8453".

salt.description: Salt is the salt the terms issued with the nonce.

signature.description: Signature is the 65-byte EIP-712 signature, 0x hex.

atPeriodEnd.description:
AtPeriodEnd cancels at the end of the paid period rather than at once. It
defaults TRUE, because a customer who cancels has already paid for the
period they are in.

id.description: ID is the subscription, from the path.
ID is the invoice or the subscription, from the path.

token.description: Token is the shared payment token (spt_...) the buyer granted.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is how much to charge, in cents of Currency. Required.

billingPhone.description:
Phone and Billing are what the buyer typed in the payment form; their name and
email are the identity's, never a field here. They come after every older
field so the plane layout of those fields holds across a rollout.

currency.description:
Currency is the ISO-4217 code to charge in. Empty takes the deployment's
own default.

paymentMethodId.description: MethodID names a card the subject already saved, for the saved-card endpoint.

provider.description:
Provider names the explicit payment processor ("square" or "paypal") when
SourceID is a provider-specific order/token (e.g. a PayPal v2 Order ID).

sourceId.description:
SourceID is a single-use card token from the payment form, for the token
endpoint. It is vaulted as part of the charge, so a caller never holds card
numbers and this service never sees one.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is the dollars of credit to buy, in cents.

billingPhone.description: Phone and Billing are what the buyer typed in the payment form.

country.description: Country is the buyer's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country; the edge's geo country when absent.

currency.description: Currency is the currency the buyer chose to pay in; empty takes the country's default.

method.description: Method is the payment method the buyer chose, when they have.

planId.description: Optional plan fields when paying a plan's first period via bank transfer (ACH).

account.description:
Account is the wallet the debit drew from, the same key GET
/v1/billing/balance reports for this caller.

amount.description: Amount is the debit, exactly as recorded.

id.description: ID is the act's name, echoed.

org.description: Org is the organization whose ledger holds the debit.

amount.description:
Amount is what the act costs, as an exact decimal in USD. It must be
greater than zero.

id.description:
ID names the act, chosen by the reporting application and stable across its
retries: the ledger debits one act once. At most 128 printable characters,
no whitespace. Reusing an ID for a different amount is a 409.

model.description:
Model names the unit the amount prices (a machine size, a model id), and is
recorded with the debit.

org.description:
Org is the organization this usage is billed to. It must be the org the
token acts in — the application's own, or one that granted it membership and
is selected with X-Org-Id — and any other is refused before money moves.

project.description:
Project attributes the debit to one project of the org. Empty is the org's
default project.

service.description:
Service scopes the debit for spend caps and attributes it to a product, as
a lowercase slug. Empty takes the reporting application's name.

amountCents.description: AmountCents is what the bank received, in cents.

bankReference.description: BankReference is the bank's own reference for the transfer.

reference.description: Reference is the reference the payer was shown beside the bank details (WIRE-...).

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
